resources.string: Show this tool on the toolbar and in the toolbox
Keyboard height, width, alignment and split
Keyboard height, width, alignment and floating mode
Keyboard height, width, alignment and one-handed mode
How the app grid orders the apps
Show each app\'s name under its icon
Show the apps you opened last in a row above the grid
The keyboard keeps the last 10 apps you opened from this tool, on your device only. Turn this off to stop the tracking and delete the list.
Press and hold an app to list its screens
With this off, press and hold pins the app instead.
Also list screens that only the app itself may open
Android does not let other apps open these screens. They show dimmed, and a press on one does nothing. Useful to explore what an app contains.
Turn plugins on, see which ones are installed, and see what each one can do
Keep the emoji button visible next to the suggestions
Suggestions, the history tab, the emoji row, skin tones and favourites
Save copied text so that you can paste it quickly
Show the last copied text as a chip on the suggestion strip. One press pastes it
Show a short \"Copied\" pop-up when you copy or cut text from the keyboard

This works for the copy actions of the keyboard: the A/C/V/X clipboard shortcuts and the copy button of the text editing panel. It works only for fields that give no copy feedback of their own. This setting is off by default.
Delete unpinned clips after this time
How many unpinned clips the history keeps

This is the second limit on the history. The clipboard expiry above is the first one. A busy day of copying can make hundreds of clips well inside the expiry time. When the panel is full, each new copy deletes the oldest unpinned clip. Pinned clips do not count against this limit, and the keyboard never deletes them.
Show an abc, space and backspace row at the bottom of the clipboard panel, like the emoji panel
Hide the toolbar behind a back button so the history gets the whole keyboard

The clipboard panel takes the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row step aside, and a slim back header takes their place. The history then shows more clips at once. While you search the history, the panel returns to its compact form so the keys fit below it. This setting is off by default.
List pinned clips at the end of the panel instead of the top
Show a search bar at the top of the clipboard panel. It filters the history as you type
Take one-time codes, phone numbers and links out of your clips. Each one becomes its own chip

The chips sit above the history in dashed outlines, so they read as parts of a clip and not as clips of their own. Press and hold a chip to see it marked inside the clip that it comes from. A press pastes only that part, and the clip stays in the history. The keyboard finds these parts on your device.
Forget after you paste a password
Delete a clip from the history and from the system clipboard as soon as you paste it into a password field

Every app on your device can read the system clipboard. Without this setting, a password from a password manager stays readable there until it expires. This applies to the pastes that you make with the keyboard into a password field: the clipboard panel, the paste chip, hold V and Ctrl+V. This setting is on by default.
Get the page title of a copied link and show it in the panel. This contacts the linked site
Show your screenshots in the clipboard next to copied text and images
The app needs the storage permission
Open the system settings to give the permission
Record which app a clip comes from. Press and hold a clip to see it. This needs the Usage Access permission

The keyboard reads the app in the foreground at the moment you copy, through Usage Access. Some copies have no source app, for example a copy from a background sync. Nothing about your app usage leaves your device.
The app needs the Usage Access permission
Without it, the keyboard saves clips with no source app
What to do with a copied password or one-time code

Android lets an app mark what it puts on the clipboard as sensitive. A password manager does this when you copy a login. Nothing else on your device acts on that mark, so the keyboard acts on it here. A hidden clip shows as dots in the panel. The keyboard never offers it as a paste chip and never puts it in a settings backup. It deletes itself on the short timer below and not on the history expiry. If you pin the clip, none of that applies, because a pin means \"keep this\".
Also treat a clip that looks like a password or a bare verification code as sensitive, not only the clips that the copying app marks

Most password managers are older than the sensitive mark of Android, and a code that you copy by hand out of a message carries no mark at all. The keyboard looks for these clips on your device, and the test is narrow on purpose. A clip matches only when the whole clip is one token: a short run of capital letters and digits, or a long mix of capital letters, small letters, digits and symbols. Sentences, links and email addresses never match.
This time is separate from the history expiry above
Width of the gap between the two halves
You can also drag the corner grip of the panel to change this
Turn the torch off when the keyboard closes

On: the torch goes off when the keyboard closes or when you change apps, so it is never left on in your pocket. Off: the torch stays on until you turn it off again, from the tool or from the quick settings tile of the system.
Show the heading in numbers under the compass rose
Mark the direction of the Kaaba on the compass

The keyboard computes the qibla bearing from the location that you save in the weather tool. The two tools share that location. The keyboard computes everything on your device, and the compass never uses the network.
No location is saved yet. Set one under Tools → Weather.
Show the pitch and the roll in degrees under the bubble
Both shortcuts are standard for redo. Which one works depends on the app that you type in. If redo does nothing, try the other one.
Show the moon the way it looks south of the equator
The weather and the place search both use Open-Meteo, only when you use them. The keyboard makes no other network requests.
Its day number also shows inside each day cell
The keyboard shows it in the header and under the selected day
Move the computed Hijri date to match the local moon sighting

The tool uses the arithmetic (tabular) Hijri calendar. Real Islamic months start at the sighting of the crescent moon. That can differ from the tables by one or two days. Set the offset that matches your local authority.

Select any two calendars to show next to the Gregorian one. The keyboard computes Chinese dates from astronomy. The Hebrew, Persian, Hindu (Saka), Buddhist and Japanese calendars are exact arithmetic. Hijri is the tabular calendar, so it has the day offset above.\n\nAll three start from the region of your device: the Bengali calendar in Bangladesh, era years in Japan, a Friday and Saturday weekend across much of the Middle East. That is only a guess at what you want. You can change all of it here.
Press a day to see its events from the calendar of your device. The keyboard asks for calendar access the first time that you open the tool. It only reads events and never changes them.
Open the tool on the front camera instead of the back one
Save front camera photos the way the preview shows them

Camera sensors record selfies without a mirror. The text then reads correctly, but the photo looks turned around next to the preview. On: the saved photo matches what you saw while you framed it. Off: the keyboard keeps the true orientation of the sensor.
Also keep photos in Pictures/WM Keyboard
This setting is off by default, because photos that you take here are normally one-time sends and not photos to keep. On: the keyboard copies every photo into the gallery and also sends it.
Keep the full 4:3 picture instead of the part in the viewfinder

The viewfinder is as wide as the keyboard, so the top and the bottom of the picture go off the screen. The keyboard usually cuts those parts away, and you send what you saw. On: you send the full 4:3 photo, which holds more than the viewfinder showed you. The preview does not change.
Play the camera click when you take a photo
Vibrate on the shutter, the controls and the timer countdown
This uses the haptic style and strength of the keyboard, under Typing → Feedback. If the keyboard haptics are off, the camera tool stays silent too.

The keyboard cuts photos down to what the viewfinder shows, saves them in the private storage of the app and sends them into the chat. Nothing goes into your gallery, and the camera runs only while the tool is open.\n\nTurn on “Send the whole photo” if you want the full 4:3 picture and not only the part in the viewfinder.
Look up the word at the cursor
The tool searches the selected word or the current word when it opens
Definitions come from the Free Dictionary API (dictionaryapi.dev). The keyboard sends the word that you look up to that service, only when you use the tool.
Pause between repeats while you hold an arrow or backspace. A lower value is faster
7 8 9 on the top row, like a desk keypad. Off puts 1 2 3 on top, like a dialer
The keyboard learns no words and no emoji habits from your typing
Copies do not go into the history of the clipboard tool
Turn on by itself in incognito tabs and private fields
Press the tool to turn incognito on. Press it again to go back to normal typing. This is the same switch as Settings → Privacy.
The same switch that the toolbar tool uses

This drops the features below until you turn it off again. It stays on after a restart and at any battery level. A full battery does not turn it off.\n\nNothing is lost. The features come back exactly as you had them, because power saving never rewrites your settings. It only hides them while it is on.
As well as the switch above
\"Android battery saver\" follows the system switch, so the keyboard saves power exactly when you already asked your device to. \"Battery is low\" uses your own percentage below instead.
Power saving starts at this level or below it
Ignore the automatic triggers while the charger is in
There is nothing to save while the battery fills, so the automatic triggers stop. This does not change the switch above. If you turn power saving on by hand, it stays on.
Stop transitions and motion, as reduced motion does
Stop drawing the trail behind a swiped word
This drops only the trail. Glide typing still works. The keyboard draws the trail on every frame of a gesture, so it costs more than the decode that it decorates.
Stop the character bubble over each key
A swipe decode is the most expensive thing the keyboard does. It is also why many people use the keyboard, so this setting is off by default and only the trail is dropped.
Stop reading what you type for emoji to offer
Stop matching sums, conversions and tool keywords as you type
No link previews and no automatic look-ups

This stops the requests that happen without you asking: previews for copied links and for scanned QR codes, and the look-up of the dictionary when you select a word. Tools that you open yourself still work, such as translate, search and GIFs.
Stop watching for new screenshots to offer in the clipboard
Use the system recognizer for voice typing, and glide a word instead of writing it

Offline voice typing and handwriting both run a neural model on the processor, which is the most expensive work the keyboard does. Voice typing goes back to the system recognizer, and the letter swipe goes back to glide typing.
Power saving is a view of your settings and never a rewrite of them. Everything that it turns off here comes back exactly as you had it the moment power saving ends.
The tool uses this same switch. You can also find it under Typing
Suggestions, autocorrect, capital letters and more
Haptic style and strength, key preview, press and hold
The haptic style and strength are under Key press → Haptic feedback. The panel of the tool changes the same settings from the keyboard.
Only an S Pen or another stylus draws. The keyboard ignores finger touches
This helps to reject the palm while you write with a stylus. Even with this setting off, the keyboard ignores finger touches for a short time after stylus strokes, so a resting palm does not draw.
Put a space between words that you write one after another
How long after the last stroke the keyboard waits before it recognizes the word
A shorter pause feels faster, but it can cut multi-stroke letters and Bengali conjuncts in half. A longer pause gives you more time between strokes. Gboard uses about half a second.
One model for each language that you type in. Recognition runs fully on your device with Google ML Kit. Each language needs a one-time download of about 20 MB. After that, handwriting works offline.
Add a language to get its handwriting model here
Create, edit, import and export keyboard themes
Without a key, translation uses the free public endpoint of Google

The keyboard sends the text that you translate to Google either way, and only while the translate panel is open. The free endpoint is unofficial and rate limited. A Cloud Translation key makes it official and reliable.
Make, edit, import and export your own packs
Hide the toolbar and move the search up next to a back button

The GIF and sticker panels take the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row step aside, and the search box moves into the row that they leave. The grid then gets every pixel. This applies to both tools.
Free from partner.klipy.com. The Tenor API closed in the middle of 2026
The GIF and sticker tools share all of this, and the content filter below. Any one key is enough. Every source that has a key shows up in the panel.
What the sticker tool gives to the chat app

Android has no sticker mark. The only signal is the MIME type of the file, and the receiving app decides. Sticker: the keyboard offers the WhatsApp sticker type first, so stickers arrive as real stickers there. Apps that do not support it get a normal image. Image: the keyboard always sends a plain image.
Images by default, because most chat apps animate them

Sticker mode works only for GIFs that the source gives in WebP form. Android ships no encoder for animated WebP, so the keyboard cannot turn a real animated GIF into a sticker. Those GIFs always go out as images.
Tabs: one chip for each source on the panel. Mixed: one grid with the results from every source mixed evenly.
High hides the most and Off hides nothing. This maps to the rating of Klipy and GIPHY, where High is G and Off is R.
From api-dashboard.search.brave.com, with a free monthly credit

Web search and image search share everything here. They search the whole web. The Brave plan includes a free monthly credit of about a thousand searches. Brave asks for attribution, so the panel shows \"via Brave\".
Each search uses one API request either way
Deselect words to cut the capture down. Off starts empty, and you select the words one by one

Recognition runs on your device with ML Kit. No photo and no text leaves your device, and it works offline. It reads Latin script text, for example English. The text recognizer of ML Kit does not support Bengali yet. After a capture, press words to select exactly what the keyboard types or copies.
Type the text of the code as soon as the keyboard finds one, with no confirm press
A short buzz when the keyboard finds a code
When a code is a web link, get the page title and description and show them above it. This needs an internet connection

Decoding runs on your device with ML Kit. It works offline and uploads nothing. It reads QR codes and the common product barcode formats, such as EAN, UPC and Code 128. Insert types the text of the code at the cursor. A link also gets an Open button.
Also keep scanned pages in Pictures/WM Keyboard

This opens the document scanner of Google, which is part of Google Play services, with edge detection, crop and shadow cleanup. Scanned pages come back as images. The keyboard puts them into the chat like a camera photo when it opens again. The processing runs on your device.
How the keyboard turns speech into text

The system recognizer is fast and shows the words while you speak, but it depends on the operating system and its languages. Offline Whisper runs fully on your device across many languages and sends no audio anywhere. It transcribes each phrase after you stop speaking.
Speak over the keys instead of in a full panel
Start the next sentence automatically after each one goes into the field
Say \"comma\", \"question mark\" or \"দাঁড়ি\" to type the mark
Speak any language and type its English translation

Recognition uses the speech recognizer of your device. On Android 12 and later it runs on your device when the language model is installed. If it is not, the audio goes to the recognizer service while you speak. Press and hold the microphone to speak in walkie-talkie style. It stops when you let go.
The spelling and style rules to check against
Pause after you stop typing before the issues refresh. A lower value feels faster, a higher value does less work
Set WM Keyboard as the spell checker of Android
Mark the spelling mistakes but offer no corrections

Grammar checking runs on your device with the Harper engine, the same one behind harper-ls. It works offline and uploads nothing that you type. Open the tool while you write to see the issues with one-press fixes. The dialect chip on the panel also changes the dialect.\n\nHarper can also act as the system spell checker of Android. The underlines and correction menus inside other apps then come from it as well. The button above opens the system Spell checker screen. Select WM Keyboard there. It follows the dialect that you select above. If your device hides that screen, the button opens the input method settings instead.
Subdomain code: en, bn, de, fr, es …
Insert links as [Title](url) instead of the plain address
The searches and the article text come from the free APIs of wikipedia.org, only while you use the tool.
Fractions, math operators, Greek letters, arrows, currency signs, superscripts, subscripts and typographic marks. Everything types on your device, like a normal key.
Offer the result on the suggestion strip when you type a sum

If you type \"12*4\", the keyboard puts 48 on the suggestion strip. Press it to replace the sum with the answer. If you end with \"=\", the keyboard adds the answer and keeps the sum. It ignores runs that can be dates (12/04) or phone numbers, unless you type the \"=\" yourself. This needs \"Smart chips\" on, under Typing.
Trigonometry functions use degrees. Off uses radians
Maximum number of decimal places. The unit converter uses it too
Offer the conversion on the suggestion strip when you type a measurement

If you type \"1 ft\" or \"1ft\", the keyboard puts the same length in metres on the suggestion strip. The button on the chip opens the converter on that category, with the pair and the amount already filled in. The unit that it converts into is the one that you paired it with last here. One-letter abbreviations count only when you write them against the number, so \"30c\" counts and \"30 c\" does not. Ordinary sentences stay untouched. This needs \"Smart chips\" on, under Typing.

There are 14 categories: length, mass, temperature, area, volume, speed, time, data, energy, power, pressure, angle, frequency and fuel economy. All conversions run on your device. The result precision follows the calculator setting. The panel opens again on the category and the units that you used last.
Offer the amount in %1$s when you type one in another currency

\"150 usd\", \"150usd\", \"150$\" and \"150 dollars\" all put the converted amount on the suggestion strip. The keyboard converts into the \"to\" currency of the pair below. If you type an amount that is already in that currency, it converts into the \"from\" one. The rate fetch starts when you type an amount, and nothing is requested before that.
How long a fetched exchange rate stays fresh
The upstream rates update about one time each day. A value below 24 hours mostly changes how soon the keyboard tries a failed fetch again.

Rates come from open.er-api.com, which has about 160 currencies and updates daily. frankfurter.app (European Central Bank) is the fallback. Both are free and need no API key. The keyboard remembers the from and to pair that you select on the panel.
Side length of the PNG that the keyboard inserts
QR codes go out as images by default

Some chat apps draw a plain incoming image with no bubble. That can look like a sticker, even though it was sent as an image. Sticker mode offers the WhatsApp sticker type instead, where the app supports it.
Also keep generated codes in Pictures/WM Keyboard
Higher levels survive more dirt and damage but hold less text. The keyboard generates the code on your device and follows what the text field contains.
Between words, for example - or . Leave it blank for none
The keyboard adds it to a random word
The keyboard generates everything on your device with a cryptographic random source. It never stores it and never logs it. Passphrase words come from the bundled English word list of the keyboard.
Setups for each app and each field, and what each one changes
